name: What evidence is needed to prove a misdiagnosis case?

mainEntity.name: What evidence is needed to prove a misdiagnosis case?

acceptedAnswer.text: To prove a misdiagnosis case, you typically need to establish four key elements: a doctor-patient relationship, demonstrating a duty of care; a breach of that duty, meaning the healthcare professional failed to meet the accepted standard of care; causation, linking the breach directly to your injury or worsened condition; and damages, showing you suffered actual harm. Evidence commonly includes comprehensive medical records, expert witness testimony from other medical professionals explaining the standard of care and how it was breached, diagnostic test results, witness statements, and documentation of your financial losses and suffering.
acceptedAnswer.description: Evidence needed includes medical records, expert witness testimony, diagnostic test results, and documentation of damages to prove duty, breach, causation, and harm.
